items.title: 6.9.3 Calculating the enthalpy change of solution

source_refs.note: Topic 6.9.3, printed pages 133-134 (Figure 6.7); Sample Problem 6.8. The print labels the final answer 'delta Hhyd [NaF]' where delta Hsol is meant.

blocks.text: The enthalpy change of solution, or of hydration, can be calculated by constructing an enthalpy cycle and using Hess's law. The gaseous ions form the ionic solid (lattice energy) and the ionic solid dissolves (enthalpy of solution); the gaseous ions also go directly to ions in aqueous solution (enthalpy of hydration of cation and anion). From the cycle, delta Hlatt + delta Hsol = delta Hhyd.

blocks.alt: Left: a sodium ion ringed by four water molecules with their oxygen ends inward, notes on hydration and lattice energy, and a small schematic chart of alkali halide lattice energies falling from fluoride to iodide. Right: a triangle of boxes, gaseous ions at the top, NaF solid at the bottom left and aqueous ions at the bottom right, with the lattice, hydration and solution arrows and the Sample 6.8 numbers.
blocks.caption: Hydration, lattice energy trends and the energy cycle of solution for sodium fluoride (original diagram after Figures 6.5 to 6.7 and Sample Problem 6.8).
blocks.long_description: Water molecules point their delta- oxygen ends at a cation (and their delta+ hydrogens at an anion), releasing the hydration energy, which grows with the ion's charge density. The lattice energy released when gaseous ions form the solid falls as the ions grow and rises steeply with their charge. Two routes lead from the gaseous ions to the aqueous ions, so lattice energy plus enthalpy of solution equals the hydration energy; for NaF, (-406 - 506) - (-902) gives a delta Hsol of -10 kJ per mol.

blocks.prompt: For NaCl the lattice energy is -787 kJ per mol and the hydration enthalpies of Na+ and Cl- are -406 and -364 kJ per mol. Calculate delta Hsol and compare it with Table 6.2.
blocks.explanation: Delta Hsol = delta Hhyd - delta Hlatt = (-406 - 364) - (-787) = -770 + 787 = +17 kJ per mol by these figures, endothermic like the table's 4.98 kJ per mol; the exact value depends on the data used, but the sign agrees: the lattice energy slightly exceeds the hydration energy.

items: Energy cycle: delta Hlatt + delta Hsol = delta Hhyd, so delta Hsol = delta Hhyd - delta Hlatt; NaF: (-406 - 506) - (-902) = -10 kJ per mol.
